classes.definition: The conclusion, or a statement that depends on it, is used as a premise.
RH or an equivalent (Robin, Li positivity, Nyman–Beurling density, Λ ≤ 0, ...) is used inside the argument.
Division by a quantity that can vanish at exactly the points under study.
Interchange of limits, sums or integrals, or use of a series/product outside its region of convergence, without justification.
Finite numerical verification promoted to a statement about all cases.
The Euler product is used for Re(s) ≤ 1.
A positive-proportion or density-one statement is promoted to 'all zeros'.
A Rouché or argument-principle step relies on a bound that is not established.
A sign or normalization error in a Li/Keiper coefficient or the explicit formula.
An unstated uniformity assumption, e.g. in an ε → 0 limit of the de Bruijn–Newman route.
A rewritten pattern of a historical failed proof (never a verbatim copy).
